summary: Proposes adding a new event and signal package to the Media Gateway Control Protocol, to control an Audio Resource Function that may reside on a media gateway or specialized audio server. It is an informational memo.

eli5.summary: This is a proposal to add new buttons to a phone-call controller, so it can tell an audio machine to play and record sounds.

questions: what is ivr interactive voice response
how does playback and collection work
subtitle: A proposal to add audio playback and recording capabilities to the Media Gateway Control Protocol.

tldr.problem: Media Gateway Control Protocol (MGCP) needed support for interactive voice response (IVR) operations like playing announcements, collecting DTMF digits, and recording user speech, with flexible audio management.
tldr.mechanism: This proposal adds an Advanced Audio Package to MGCP with three main events: PlayAnnouncement (plays audio without user interaction), PlayCollect (plays a prompt and collects DTMF digits), and PlayRecord (plays a prompt and records speech). The package supports direct references to simple audio, references to complex provisioned audio structures, audio variables, and user-defined qualifiers like language and speaker.
tldr.outcome: The proposal allows MGCP-controlled systems to implement sophisticated IVR applications that can combine announcements, collect user input, and handle multilingual audio. It supports both provisioned audio structures and dynamic audio composition.

facts.label: Nesting support
facts.value: Sets and sequences can be nested

today: RFC 2897 is an Informational memo (not a standards-track document) published in August 2000. It represents a proposal for extending MGCP with audio capabilities. The proposal has not been adopted as an Internet standard, but similar audio and IVR capabilities have been integrated into subsequent protocols and implementations.

sections.title: Audio Control for Phone Systems
sections.content:
This document proposes adding audio capabilities to the Media Gateway Control Protocol (MGCP) to control an Audio Resource Function (ARF). The ARF can be part of a media gateway or a specialized audio server.

The proposal defines an Advanced Audio Package with three main operations: PlayAnnouncement (plays audio without waiting for user input), PlayCollect (plays a prompt and waits for the user to enter DTMF digits), and PlayRecord (plays a prompt and records the user's speech). These are the core operations of Interactive Voice Response (IVR) systems, which power phone-based customer service and automated information systems.
sections.eli5: Phone systems need to play recorded messages, ask for button presses, and record what people say. This adds those features to MGCP.

sections.title: Audio Structures and Composition
sections.content:
The proposal supports both simple and complex audio structures. A simple structure is a single recorded announcement. A complex structure combines multiple parts: announcements, voice variables (like a number read aloud), silence, tones, or other segments.

Audio can be composed in two ways: direct specification, where the protocol describes each component, or indirect reference, where the audio is provisioned on the server and only a reference identifier is passed. The proposal also introduces sequences (a provisioned sequence of mixed audio segments played in order) and sets (a provisioned collection of audio variants with an associated selector, such as language). Using selectors like language, accent, gender, or customer, the system can resolve a single audio reference to the correct variant at playback time.
sections.eli5: Audio can be simple (one recording) or complex (announcements mixed with numbers or other parts). You can also define language versions of the same message and let the system pick the right one.

sections.title: Playback and Collection Operations
sections.content:
PlayAnnouncement plays audio without monitoring the incoming media stream, making it efficient for treatments, informational announcements, and alerts.

PlayCollect plays a prompt and collects DTMF digits (0-9, *, #, and A-D). It supports reprompting if the user enters no digits or an invalid pattern. The operation can define special key sequences and key sets to recognize caller intentions like "enter to continue" or "0 for operator." By default, it makes only one attempt and has no initial prompt, functioning as a simple digit collection.

PlayRecord plays a prompt and records the user's speech. Like PlayCollect, it supports reprompting if the user does not speak and can handle multiple attempts. Recordings can be temporary (lasting only the duration of the call) or persistent (stored beyond the call for later playback or reuse).
sections.eli5: PlayAnnouncement plays a message and does nothing else. PlayCollect plays a message and waits for the user to press buttons. PlayRecord plays a message and saves what the person says back to them.

sections.title: Parameters and Signals
sections.content:
The proposal defines multiple parameters for the three main operations, with most parameters being optional and defaulting to reasonable values. Parameters allow the control agent to specify the audio reference, repetition count, digit buffer control, interruptibility rules, and retry behavior.

Two additional signals complete the package: EndSignal gracefully terminates an active Play, PlayCollect, or PlayRecord operation, returning any collected digits or the recording ID of the in-progress recording. OperationComplete is detected upon successful completion of any operation, and OperationFailed is detected when an operation fails. The proposal also specifies signal interaction rules: if an identical signal is applied to an active operation, the new signal is discarded and the original continues.
sections.eli5: Each operation has optional settings like whether to play a prompt, how many tries to allow, and how to handle pauses. Special signals can stop an operation early or signal when it finishes.

sections.title: Variables and Advanced Features
sections.content:
The proposal introduces audio variables to support dynamic content. For example, a system can combine recorded announcement "Your balance is" with a variable number "37.50" spoken aloud, followed by another announcement "dollars." Variables have a type (like NUMBER or TIME), a subtype (for formatting), and a value.

The package defines selectors to resolve complex audio at runtime. The language selector is pre-defined; user-defined selectors allow custom classification by accent, gender, speaker, customer, or any other dimension. At runtime, a reference to audio with selectors is resolved to the matching variant. Nested definitions are allowed, so a sequence can contain sets, or a set can contain sequences, enabling sophisticated hierarchical audio structures.
sections.eli5: Variables let the system plug in numbers or dates into recorded messages. Selectors like language let the system pick the right version of a message automatically.

sections.title: IVR Applications
sections.content:
The Advanced Audio Package enables realistic IVR systems. An example is an automated prepaid calling card system: it plays "There are" + the variable (number of minutes) + "minutes remaining on your prepaid calling card." Another example is a directory assistance system that can greet callers in their preferred language, ask what they are looking for, and play the result in their selected language and accent.

The proposal supports both highly dynamic systems (where each component is specified in the protocol) and efficient provisioned systems (where complex audio structures are pre-built on the server and referenced by a simple identifier). The optionality of most parameters allows applications to use minimal protocol syntax when they rely on reasonable defaults or provisioned structures.
sections.eli5: Systems using this can build sophisticated voice menus: greeting you in your language, asking what you want, and reading back information in your preferred voice.
